title: Choo-Choo-choot-‘em up
author: Bean0
selftext: Made in two weeks for a game jam about crossing genres. Hate and love welcome 🙏

comments.author: krazyjakee
comments.body: Avoid SUNO if you can as all their instruments and chord progressions are the same.

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body: Aye I’m not a big fan of gen ai music, but I had to get something decent enough in a pinch for the deadline

replies.author: Mr__Earthling
replies.body:
You do realize you can upload your own sample... You can even have gpt generate a midi file and you can change the notes yourself (gpt has midify built in)...then export it to suno...there's your unique melody. 

For intruments, you can literally tell it exactly which instrument you want (you can name specific synths, drum machines and so on)... Be... Dare I say... Creative!

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body: Ya, I’ve done it before! I’ve got lots of experience making my own music before AI. I have fed some of it before to AI like your suggestion, but like I said, tight deadlines made for some decisions that are not ideal, my priorities were split 😅

comments.author: toomanynamesaretook
comments.body: Lol fuck yeah keep cooking.

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body: Haha the menus do have drum and bass in them, it’s basically just a kind of half proof of concept stage atm. The gameplay is actually quite niche, it’s sort of a stressful shooting gallery with mad scenery, not sure how much legs it has unless I cram in some rogue like stuff or procedural levels. I just hope it does well in the game jam! And it’s probably not suited to mobile or any platform other than mouse and keyboard. Thanks for the encouragement!

comments.body: Okay this is actually pretty good, the art style is consistent - UI could ues some more work as you ahve a couple two many fonts going on. well done

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body:
Thank you! Haha the many fonts are a sort of deliberate choice. I told myself the aesthetic is ‘eclectic (but restrained) maximalism’. Getting something that felt less like most AI game UI/HUDs is a challenge.

It’s homogenized a bit for menus (limited to 3) but yeah, main HUD has incredibly individualized parts, but it honestly felt better than any alternative, although I absolutely would take any CC feedback on board if I see anything that works better. But I will continue to refine it 🙏

comments.author: odragora
comments.body:
Looks great.

What are you using for 3D assets?

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body:
Thank you! Most of the assets are generated by Claude (this wouldn’t have been possible without Opus 5.5 / Astra, the jump in quality has been insane), but I mix in some assets that were free or I had purchased before, but not that many. Most of the heavy lifting is done by the texture work, which was made with GPT 2.5 image gen.  

It’s all very lightweight, game comes in at around 26mb, mostly used for sound files. Three.js great for quick prototyping like this

replies.author: odragora
replies.body:
Thanks for the answer.

Did you use Opus 5.5 to generate assets in Three.js code, or through Blender with MCP / computer use? 

Also very curious about your texturing workflow, what do you provide GPT-Image 2.5 with? Just a model, or an environment where it can iterate over the texture, check how it looks in the engine and iterate over it to polish?

In my experience with animated 2D sprites it's pretty much impossible to achieve a good result one-shot, but maybe it's easier with textures.

replies.author: Bean0
replies.body:
I didn’t involve blender too much with this, as it’s easier to just run it native through the client I find. Using blender with MCP is more something I’ve done with using unity, and I would do it for something more substantial maybe. But also I like to hand make stuff if I have the time, as low poly is almost quicker to learn to do some stuff manually, and get AI to do grunt work like sorting files or even setting up the file. 

I did use Astra with mcp and aseprite, for a fair amount of 2d textures and pixel art, it’s not perfect but it did sooo much. Like tree sprites and bushes with transparent backgrounds, animatable elements on different layers. 

And yeah, almost nothing is one shot here, Many iterations. Which is always the way imo.
